cases.doc: Indicates all possible `token_id`s are already in use.
cases.name: TokenIDsAreDepleted

cases.doc: Indicates the token was already minted.
cases.name: TokenAlreadyMinted

cases.doc: Indicates the token was already claimed. Dead: `claim` is gone \xe2\x80\x94 `mint` binds the\ntoken to the card's purse in the same call, so there is no second step to repeat.\nKept so the discriminant is not reused.
cases.name: TokenAlreadyClaimed

cases.doc: Indicates the token exists but has no owner. Not reachable for a token this wasm\nminted, since `mint` writes the owner; only for one minted by a pre-merge wasm on\na deployment upgraded in place.
cases.name: TokenNotClaimed

cases.doc: Curve was not stored for this chip (must be set at mint).
cases.name: MissingCurve

cases.doc: Destination account does not list this card as a signer. Dead: no path raises it\nany more, since `claim` binds to the card's own purse and consults no account.\nKept so the discriminant is not reused.
cases.name: NotCardHolder

cases.doc: The pocket factory is unset, so there is no purse to deploy the card's token to.\nSet it with `set_factory` before minting \xe2\x80\x94 `mint` checks this before it writes\nanything, so a mint that hits this leaves no partial state behind.
cases.name: MissingPocket

cases.doc: `trait_values` was handed more keys than one call may batch.
cases.name: TooManyTraitKeys

event_v0.doc: A card provisioned: token minted, purse deployed, the two bound. `to` is the purse \xe2\x80\x94\na token is never emitted unowned, because there is no state in which it is. The data\nis the bare token id, as SEP-50 gives it.
event_v0.name: Mint

event_v0.doc: SEP-50's metadata update, named `metadata` after the rule that an event takes its\nemitter's name: what a token's metadata says changed, so a client that cached it\nfetches it again. The data is the bare token id, as SEP-50 gives it.
event_v0.name: Metadata

event_v0.doc: A stored trait changed (SEP-50's trait update, ERC-7496 `TraitUpdated`). The token id\nis a topic, so the events of one token can be filtered.
event_v0.name: SetTrait

event_v0.doc: SEP-50 `transfer`: a token changed owner. Clawback is the only path that does it after\nmint, and the standard wants every change of owner announced, so an indexer can follow\nownership from this event alone. Mint announces itself with [`Mint`] instead.
event_v0.name: Transfer

event_v0.doc: ERC-7496 `TraitMetadataURIUpdated`: the schema every cached trait is read through.
event_v0.name: SetTraitMetadataUri

function_v0.doc:
This card's purse, or `None` when no factory is configured or no purse has been
deployed yet.

The one link an outside reader cannot reconstruct alone: `public_key(token_id)`
is public, but nothing on chain says which factory to ask. Deliberately a
*pointer* and not a balance \xe2\x80\x94 the purse holds the card's float and its DeFi
positions, and it can answer for both without this contract mirroring either.

Best-effort by design: a missing, mis-pointed or trapping factory reads as
`None`. Resolving a card must never be able to fail because of a contract this
one merely points at.
function_v0.name: pocket

function_v0.doc:
Set a stored trait. Admin only.

# Arguments

* `e` - The environment object.
* `token_id` - Token id as a number.
* `trait_key` - Name of the trait; only `tier` exists.
* `new_value` - The value to store.

# Panics

* If the admin does not authorize the call.
* If the token does not exist (`NonFungibleTokenError::NonExistentToken`).
* If the key is not a declared trait (`NonFungibleTokenError::TraitDoesNotExist`).

# Events

Two, in this order:

* topics - `["set_trait", token_id: u32]`, data - `{trait_key: String, new_value:
i128}`. SEP-50's trait update.
* topics - `["metadata"]`, data - `token_id: u32`. SEP-50's metadata update, because
`tier` drives the art, so a new value means the metadata a client cached is stale.
Mint does not emit it: nothing is cached yet.
function_v0.name: set_trait

function_v0.doc: Value of one trait, or `0` for a known trait that has never been set \xe2\x80\x94 the\nstandard's default. An unknown key is an error, not a zero.
function_v0.name: trait_value

function_v0.doc: Where the ERC-7496 trait schema lives.
function_v0.name: trait_metadata_uri

function_v0.doc:
Admin-set, so the schema can be republished without an upgrade. Emits, because
the schema is what tells a reader how to interpret every value it has cached.

# Arguments

* `e` - The environment object.
* `uri` - The new location of the trait schema.

# Panics

* If the admin does not authorize the call.

# Events

* topics - `["set_trait_metadata_uri"]`
* data - `{uri: String}`
function_v0.name: set_trait_metadata_uri

function_v0.doc:
Give each token its curve, its card's purse, and that purse as owner.

Admin-only. Every v1.0 card is secp256k1, the only curve v1.0 could verify. Purses
are deployed `Manual`, as every enrolment is: the holder opts in to ChimpDAO's
upgrades, nobody opts in for them.

Every move is a SEP-50 `transfer`: from the G-address that held the token, or, for
one never claimed, from this contract, which v1.0's `mint` event named as its owner.
An indexer then reads one unbroken ownership history per token.
function_v0.name: migrate_v1

function_v0.doc:
Stateless chip-signature oracle over the registry's stored curve. Replay is the
caller's digest contract: callers must put their own nonce/expiry inside
`digest` (the Pocket passes the host authorization payload; attestation
integrators bring a domain + nonce). Unknown cards verify false.
function_v0.name: verify_for_card

udt_union_v0.doc: Complete chip proof for one gated call (Pocket / nfc-nft).\nXDR-compatible with Earn `ChipSigData` field layout.
udt_union_v0.name: ChipAuth

udt_union_v0.doc:
What the holder wants to happen when this purse needs new code. Here rather than in
`pocket` because the factory passes it to the Pocket constructor and a `cdylib` cannot
be a library dependency.

**Enforced on the purse, recorded on the account.**

For a purse this decides how the contract holds its code. `Managed` deploys an
executable *reference* to the factory's entry, so one `set_pocket_wasm_hash` re-points
the whole fleet at once; `Pocket::upgrade` refuses under it, because pinning a hash
would leave the fleet in silence. `Manual` pins a hash that only the card's own chip
can move. That is CAP-85, and it is the second authority a gate always needed \xe2\x80\x94 the
tag owner \xe2\x80\x94 which is why this stopped being a note and became a decision.

`ChimpAccount` still only records it: accounts are deployed off-chain by a G-address,
so nothing owns an entry for them to reference.

Set at mint, before a card has a holder. The enrolment station passes `Manual`, so
following the fleet is the holder's opt-in, made later thr
udt_union_v0.name: UpgradePolicy

void_v0.doc: Holder accepts security upgrades pushed by ChimpDAO.
void_v0.name: Managed

void_v0.doc: Holder is notified and taps to accept each upgrade.
